solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Reportedly regret dig in simulated chatter on stage

indicators.note: reportedly means as said by others, so the word is taken by its spoken sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: to rue is to regret; said aloud it matches the opening syllable
a barb is a cutting remark, a dig

explanation.surface: An actor regrets having to make a pointed remark amid the fake background chatter of a crowd scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Extras on stage traditionally mutter the word over and over to sound like a murmuring crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors repeat the word to imitate indistinct crowd talk, so it names that simulated background noise.

clue.text: Oppose others touring islands

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: the rest means the others
IS is the abbreviation for islands

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers object to the rest of the party going round the islands.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to fight against or withstand, the same as opposing.

clue.text: Endure French and German articles on energy

indicators.note: in a down answer on means placed above, so the earlier pieces sit over the last one

blocks.note: un is the French indefinite article
der is a German definite article
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson on French and German articles about energy, which you simply have to put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something unpleasant is to experience and endure it.

clue.text: Legal process once secured, we're told, by King Edward

indicators.note: we're told means as heard spoken, so a word's sound is wanted, not its spelling

blocks.note: attained means secured or achieved; spoken, it matches the first seven letters
ER is Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: A historical legal procedure supposedly secured by King Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: Attainder stripped a person condemned for treason of all civil rights and property; it was abolished in Britain in 1870.
explanation.definitionFit: Attainder was a historic legal process of forfeiture, hence 'once' for something no longer used.

clue.text: Looked after by American woman with liberal views

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two pieces are simply set next to each other

blocks.note: broad is American slang for a woman
minded means looked after, as in minding children

explanation.surface: A child cared for by an open-minded American woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad-minded person is tolerant, holding liberal views.

clue.text: Employed regularly at first in Surrey town

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter only of the word just before it
in tells us one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: Woking is a commuter town in Surrey, south-west of London
the first letter of regularly

explanation.surface: Someone takes a job with regular hours in a Surrey commuter town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' looks like an adverb about being employed, but only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is employed has a job and is therefore in work, the adjective sense.

clue.text: Wrasse regularly used to be!

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters of wrasse

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the wrasse, a sea fish, is no more.
explanation.definitionFit: Was is the past tense of be, so it means used to be.

clue.text: Travel across top of Grampian elevation

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter
across means spanning over, so one piece stretches round the other

blocks.note: to ride is to travel
the first letter of Grampian

explanation.surface: A trek over the summit of the Grampian mountains in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grampians are a mountain range in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long narrow raised strip of land, an elevation.

clue.text: Flower arrangement president originally admired propping up bar

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word counts
in a down answer propping up means sitting underneath, so that piece comes after

blocks.note: Ike was the nickname of US President Eisenhower
to bar is to ban
the first letter of admired

explanation.surface: A president admires a flower display while leaning on a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Propping up bar' paints a drinker; in a down clue it means the letter sits below the word for bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikebana is the Japanese art of arranging flowers.

clue.text: Blokes adopting a jolly set of clothes

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so one piece is absorbed into the other

blocks.note: gents are men, blokes
taken as written
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: Men take on a cheerful outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an adjective for the clothes; it is a noun, an old naval nickname for a marine.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments are articles of clothing, together making up an outfit.

clue.text: Disloyal ultimately thus to amend promissory notes

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the closing letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: the last letter of thus
to edit a text is to amend it
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: Someone decides in the end to alter their IOUs, a dishonest piece of book-keeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Seditious speech or action incites rebellion against the state, so it is disloyal to it.

clue.text: Dull, but finally played minster organ

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so the last letter of each of the next two words is taken

blocks.note: the last letter of played
the last letter of minster
the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A cathedral organ recital that ended up being boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the instrument in a minster; here it is a body part. 'Finally' governs both played and minster.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a literary form of dreary, meaning gloomy and dull.

clue.text: Exotic inn accommodating artist in Lambeth Palace area

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so one piece holds the other inside it

blocks.note: Lambeth Palace is in the London postal district SE1, with the 1 written as I
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A foreign-style inn near the Archbishop of Canterbury's London residence puts up a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Lambeth Palace, the Archbishop of Canterbury's London home, has the postcode SE1.
explanation.definitionFit: A serai is a caravanserai, a travellers' inn in the Middle East or Asia, so exotic to a Briton.

clue.text: Frantic burst of speed leading to charge

indicators.note: something burst is broken apart, so its letters are scattered and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: A frantic sprint that ends in a cavalry-style charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burst of speed' reads as one phrase, but 'burst' works on the letters of speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone desperate acts in a frantic, reckless way out of hopelessness.

clue.text: Fellow dropping art damages joint position at college

indicators.note: dropping means letting fall, so some letters are removed from the name

blocks.note: Stuart is a man's name, a fellow
taken as written, the letters to remove
dents are damage, as verb and noun
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: An academic fellow gives up art and hurts his hip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow' and 'position at college' both suggest academia, but the fellow is just a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A studentship is a funded post or scholarship for a student at a university.

clue.text: See way lessee keeps place for crown representative

indicators.note: keeps here just places the tenant alongside the location, so they sit next to one another

blocks.note: lo is an old word for look or see
RD is the abbreviation for road
lieu means place, as in 'in lieu of'
a lessee holds a lease, so is a tenant

explanation.surface: Instructions to inspect how a leaseholder keeps a property.
explanation.walkthrough: The tenant 'keeps' the place only loosely: the pieces simply follow one another, the place before the lessee.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lord Lieutenant is the monarch's personal representative in a British county.

clue.text: African national primarily involved in playing the piano

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the first letter of the next word is used
playing suggests the letters are played about with and rearranged

blocks.note: the first letter of involved
taken as written

explanation.surface: An African citizen is mainly occupied with playing the piano.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ethiopian is a citizen of Ethiopia, a country in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Scholarly friend in Paris caught sheltering rebel

indicators.note: sheltering means giving cover to, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: ami is French for friend
Jack Cade led a rebellion in Kent in 1450
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A Parisian friend is arrested for harbouring a rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: Academic means relating to learning and study, the adjective sense of scholarly.

clue.text: Eccentric English poet, he, transfixed by Irish county

indicators.note: transfixed means pierced right through, so one piece is driven into the middle of the other

blocks.note: a cam is an eccentric, an off-centre wheel on a rotating shaft
Robert Bridges was an English Poet Laureate
taken as written
IR is an abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: An odd English poet is pinned down in an Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' looks like an adjective for the poet but is a noun, the engineering part.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridgeshire is an English county in East Anglia; the clue's 'Irish' is a decoy for location.

clue.text: Badly-treated girl embracing aristocratic boy

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: a miss is a girl
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U usage
Ed is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl hugging a posh boy who has been badly treated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'U' for upper-class comes from a 1950s essay on U and non-U English usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something misused has been used wrongly or abused, so badly treated.

clue.text: Think about French leader suppressing the French court

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
in a down answer suppressing means pressing down on top, so that piece comes above

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
the first letter of French
le is French for the
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Pondering a French politician who silences a French court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Think about' looks like the whole definition, but 'about' is part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To reflect is to think carefully, ponder.

clue.text: It expunges Times leader dismissing heavy metal

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so some letters leave the word

blocks.note: eras are times, periods
taken as written
lead is a heavy metal

explanation.surface: A Times editorial is deleted after it sacks a rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times leader' suggests a newspaper editorial; 'leader' is just the word, losing its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An eraser is a rubber, a tool that rubs out and so expunges writing.

clue.text: Defame prudent woman hiding second pill

indicators.note: hiding means covering over, so one item takes the place of another in the word

blocks.note: discreet means careful and prudent
Di is a woman's name, short for Diana
E is the drug ecstasy, taken as a pill; the second of the two in the synonym is meant

explanation.surface: Someone smears a careful woman by saying she concealed a second tablet.
explanation.walkthrough: The woman covers the second E of the synonym for prudent, taking its place.
explanation.definitionFit: To discredit someone is to damage their reputation, which is what defaming does.

clue.text: Like kidneys finally eaten in proper setting

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the next word
a setting surrounds what it holds, as a ring holds a stone, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: the last letter of eaten
real means proper, genuine

explanation.surface: Kidneys are at last eaten in a suitable setting for offal.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal means relating to the kidneys, the adjective for them.

clue.text: Bid dyke-builder talked of

indicators.note: talked of means mentioned in speech, so it is the spoken sound of the name that counts

blocks.note: Offa, an 8th-century king of Mercia, built Offa's Dyke along the Welsh border

explanation.surface: A bid made by someone who builds dykes, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa's Dyke is the great earthwork bank marking the old border between England and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A bid is an offer, as of a price at auction.

clue.text: Stoneworker's mother's old name

blocks.note: ma is mother, with the possessive S
O is the abbreviation for old
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A stonemason's mother's maiden name, the one she had before marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition's possessive is a trick: the 's belongs to the wordplay, with the definition just Stoneworker.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason is a craftsman who cuts and lays stone, a builder in stone.

clue.text: He scores one, oddly, but she succeeds jointly

definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for the noun

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so these letters come out in an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: In a match, he scores a single goal, but she is the one who wins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like 'only the odd letters', but here it signals the letters are scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: A coheiress is a woman who inherits jointly with others, so she succeeds to an estate with them.

clue.text: Ungentlemanly type originally courting publicity

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the first letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: the first letter of courting
an ad is an advertisement, publicity

explanation.surface: A boor who started out seeking fame.
explanation.definitionFit: A cad is a man who behaves dishonourably, especially towards women.

clue.text: Spoilt daughters left in school

indicators.note: in tells us the first pieces are placed inside the next one

blocks.note: D is daughter, doubled for the plural
L is the abbreviation for left
a coed is a coeducational school

explanation.surface: Pampered girls were abandoned at boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: A coddled child is pampered and overindulged, the past participle sense of spoilt.

clue.text: Customer outside entrance to shop, a jocular type

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its opening, so its first letter is taken
outside means one piece stands round the other, enclosing it

blocks.note: punter is British slang for a customer or client
the first letter of shop

explanation.surface: A customer loitering outside a shop door, cracking jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a punter is a customer, or someone who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A punster is a person who makes puns, a joker given to wordplay.
